sources.title: Vidal-Gadea, Rinehart & Belanger2008 — skeletal adaptations for forwards and sideways walking
sources.scope: Selected primary methods, joint/stance-swing Fig.1, comparative morphology Fig.2 and leg-morphology text viewed in author-hosted14page PDF. No raw coordinate data or quantitative joint/gait curves digitized. This study includes Carcinus maenas and two other species; their features are not interchangeable.

shape.before: Repeated smooth oval crab body, thin rod legs, oversized point eyes and indistinct front/anterolateral teeth.
shape.changed: Rear-tapered outline, five pointed anterolateral teeth per side, three frontal lobes, lower gastric/branchial relief, smaller ridged chelae with carpal-tooth cues and pale curved fingers. Eight plated articulated legs have longer middle pairs and shorter final pair with pointed tips.
shape.remaining: Unmeasured proportions and regional layout; incomplete mouth/gill/ventral anatomy. No systematic sex, life-stage or moult-state model. The last legs are slightly flattened rather than expanded into a portunid paddle.

surface.before: Nearly uniform green shading and coarse generic relief.
surface.changed: Original uneven fine granules, numerical chitin normal field, olive/tan mottling and dorsal/ventral limb distinction; surfaces remain attached through poses.
surface.remaining: The selected laboratory photo is not calibrated live-animal albedo or material data. Green through orange/red variation is documented, but this is one authored palette. It is not photogrammetry, a scan or measured chitin optics.

movement.before: One local chela gesture on fixed stick limbs; no supported walking.
movement.changed: Fixed-length articulated lateral bout with planted stance and lifted recovery, followed by settled hold. Same body/materials for local search/handling, claw opening, lowered quiet rest and Observe reset.
movement.remaining: Authored phase timing and planar IK, without imported motion coordinates, validated biological joint limits, force/neural model, continuous collision proof or prey/ingestion mechanism. No swimming action is claimed.

reviewMethod: Author inspected 42 actual final nonblank WebGL2 states on five labelled sheets against the retained Hans Hillewaert photograph, Smithsonian SERC NEMESIS species morphology and selected primary Vidal-Gadea et al. 2008 methods/figures. This is qualitative author review, not independent expert assessment or a percentage accuracy measurement.
